response.message:
I've drafted an IBM Cloud sketch for triaging synthetic security alerts. Approved logs flow through Event Streams, then a Code Engine redaction job. The redacted evidence is stored in Cloud Object Storage and indexed in OpenSearch. A triage service uses a watsonx.ai model to write a proposed response, which waits in a PostgreSQL analyst queue. Every step is recorded in an audit trail, and nothing is executed automatically.

**First local test:** we'd feed in a few synthetic alerts and use a scripted model in place of watsonx.ai. That would check that data gets redacted, that each conclusion cites its evidence, that the queue receives the proposal and that the audit trail records each step. It would not show that a real model triages well. Proving that needs a separate run against an actual watsonx.ai model with labelled test alerts. Region, account access and deployment are all still unconfirmed.

**Next question:** in which country must the alert data and logs stay? That decides which IBM regions we can consider.

proposal.title: IBM Cloud synthetic alert triage – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic alerts only; ingestion → redaction → evidence store/index → watsonx.ai triage → analyst queue with an auditable response proposal. No automated containment. Assumptions: region still to be selected; model ID, plans, quotas and account access are unverified; most components need engineering because there is no native IBM generator for them yet.

data.label: Approved log sources (synthetic)
data.description: Existing approved sources of synthetic security alerts and logs. Outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Asset context (CMDB export)
data.description: Existing asset inventory (owner, criticality, location). Read-only reference.

data.label: Alert ingestion
data.description: Kafka topics for raw alerts and asset updates, plus a dead-letter topic for alerts that fail processing.

data.label: Redaction & normalisation
data.description: Consumer job that normalises alerts, joins asset context and masks sensitive fields. Failures are quarantined. Treats all content as untrusted.

data.label: Redacted evidence store
data.description: Private bucket holding redacted evidence, with object versioning and retention to be confirmed.

data.label: Evidence retrieval index
data.description: Keyword (and later optionally vector) search over redacted evidence by alert, host and user; returns citations.

data.label: AI triage service
data.description: Retrieves evidence, calls the model, validates the structured verdict (severity, rationale, citations, proposed response) and abstains when evidence is insufficient. Read-only; has no permission to isolate hosts, disable users or execute anything.

data.label: Triage model
data.description: Foundation model inference. Model ID, regional availability and entitlement are unverified. A scripted model replaces it in local tests.

data.label: Analyst queue & case records
data.description: Stores triage cases with proposed responses and their status (pending, accepted, rejected). Proposals are never executed by the system.

data.label: SOC analyst
data.description: Reviews each proposal and decides. Any containment is done manually in existing tools.

data.label: Audit trail
data.description: Records triage events, model calls, analyst decisions and control-plane activity. Retention is to be confirmed.

requirementDrafts.statement: The system must only propose responses; host isolation, user disabling and payload execution are never performed automatically and require analyst action outside the system.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Limits exposure of sensitive fields to the model and the search index.
requirementDrafts.basis: User requested redaction within ingestion; diagram components redact, index and model.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: all log and asset data is redacted before it is indexed or sent to the model, and redaction failures are quarantined rather than passed on.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Makes every proposal reviewable and reproducible. Retention period is still to be confirmed.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: each triage records the alert ID, evidence citations, model ID, prompt version, the proposal and the analyst's decision in a tamper-evident audit trail.

response.message: Good news first: the check found no wrong connections and no failed tests. The architecture is complete and joined up end to end. The 8 blockers have two causes, and neither is a design mistake. The 2 existing sources (logs and asset context) need a plan for how we reference or import them. The other 6 IBM components (Event Streams, Code Engine redaction and triage, Object Storage, OpenSearch and watsonx.ai) have no supported generator contract yet. The only IBM contract available today is private object storage. Applying it to the evidence store wouldn't fix the main gap, and narrowing the scope to storage would break what you asked for. So there's no supported graph correction to make right now. Closing these gaps is product engineering work: native IBM implementations for Event Streams, Code Engine, OpenSearch and watsonx.ai, with this design revision 2 (artifact 5dd2d956…) as the test case. So I'm leaving the diagram as it is, with every requirement and safeguard still open, and nothing has been deployed or checked against a real model. To plan how we reference those two existing sources, how do the synthetic alerts and the CMDB export reach us today: pushed to a Kafka topic, dropped as files, or pulled from an API?
